package_info.why_malicious: These versions of Apache Tomcat contain a critical vulnerability (CVE-2019-0232) that allows remote code execution. The flaw arises from improper input sanitization and unsafe command construction in the CGI Servlet, particularly on Windows systems. Attackers can exploit this to execute arbitrary system commands with the privileges of the Tomcat process, leading to full system compromise.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the CGI Servlet processes an HTTP request and invokes a CGI script
required_permissions: filesystem access (to read/write files and execute scripts)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: This code constructs a command line argument string for process execution by directly incorporating user-supplied input (the 'command' variable). If the command contains spaces, it is wrapped in quotes. The lack of input validation or sanitization allows attackers to inject arbitrary commands.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code directly uses user-controlled input from HTTP requests to build a command string for process execution, without any sanitization or validation. This enables attackers to inject malicious commands, resulting in command injection vulnerabilities.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Secure implementations should always sanitize or strictly validate user input before using it in command execution. Here, the input is used verbatim, violating the principle of input validation and safe command construction.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate CGI Servlet implementations may construct command lines from user input, but must always sanitize and validate the input to prevent injection. The absence of such checks here is what makes this code dangerous.
key_indicators: Direct use of HTTP request parameters in command execution
No input validation or sanitization on the 'command' variable
Command string construction logic that wraps user input in quotes if it contains spaces
Process execution initiated by the servlet using user-supplied data

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP request to the Tomcat CGI Servlet, supplying malicious input in the 'command' parameter.
attack_chain.leads_to: Unsanitized input is incorporated into the command line.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable code in the CGI Servlet constructs a command string using the supplied input and executes it on the Windows system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary command execution on the server.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains remote code execution, potentially compromising the entire system.

behavioral_signatures: CGI Servlet invocation with command parameters containing suspicious or shell metacharacters
Process execution events where Tomcat is the parent process and command-line arguments are derived from HTTP request data
Unexpected child processes spawned by Tomcat on Windows systems, especially with arguments matching HTTP request patterns
file_indicators: Presence of vulnerable versions of org.apache.tomcat:tomcat-catalina or org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core in application dependencies
Tomcat configuration files (web.xml or context.xml) enabling the CGI Servlet
CGI Servlet configuration with 'enableCmdLineArguments' set to true
network_indicators: Unusual outbound network connections initiated by Tomcat child processes
HTTP requests to /cgi-bin/ or other CGI endpoints with command injection payloads (e.g., use of shell metacharacters like &, |, ; in parameters)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor process creation events where Tomcat is the parent and the command line includes arguments from HTTP requests. Audit Tomcat configuration for CGI Servlet usage and check if 'enableCmdLineArguments' is enabled. Use vulnerability scanners to identify affected Tomcat versions. Inspect HTTP logs for requests to CGI endpoints containing command injection patterns. Correlate suspicious process executions with incoming HTTP requests to CGI endpoints.
